name: Agor (by Preset)

hlido_opinion.headline: A 'multiplayer AI' workspace that puts team and agents on one shared board — strong operate/governance thinking and a real agent surface, with the usual unknowns of an unexercised product.
hlido_opinion.body: Agor, from Preset, reframes agent work as multiplayer: instead of ten private terminals, a team shares live spatial boards where sessions, prompts and costs are visible, cards 'glow' when an agent needs a human, and useful practices become shareable workflows. It layers an operate story (a command center for running many agents) and a trust story (governance over who can do what, a security page with a roadmap) on top — which is more maturity than most entrants show. It is built on harnesses teams already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Cursor), ships a managed Agor Cloud and an open-source Community Edition with a documented daemon REST API, and integrates where teams work (Slack, Discord, GitHub, Shortcut). The concept leans slightly abstract and the on-page interactions are illustrative mockups, so the real test is install-and-use, which we did not do. Cloud pricing is also gated behind 'talk to us'. A thoughtfully-built collaboration layer with a credible operator and a genuine agent-integration path.

tier_rationale: STEADY (76): mature feature set (boards, sessions, command center, governance, security), an open-source CE with a REST API, multi-harness support and a reputable operator. Short of higher bands because interactions shown are illustrative, the product was not exercised, and Cloud pricing is not disclosed.
what_it_does_well: Shared, multiplayer boards that make agent sessions, cost and 'what needs a human' visible to the whole team
Operate and governance layers (command center, who-can-do-what controls, a security page with a roadmap)
Works on harnesses teams already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Cursor) with no lock-in
Open-source Community Edition with a documented daemon REST API alongside a managed Cloud
what_it_fails_at: On-page product interactions are illustrative mockups, not an exercisable demo
Cloud pricing is gated behind 'talk to us' / book-a-demo
The 'multiplayer AI' framing is somewhat abstract until you install and use it
best_for: Teams running many agents who need shared visibility, governance and a command center
Groups that want to share prompts/workflows rather than keep them in private terminals
Orgs standardising on multiple coding harnesses who want one workspace over them
not_recommended_for: Solo users who do not need multiplayer/shared-board collaboration
Buyers who need upfront Cloud pricing before evaluating

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Community Edition exposes a daemon REST API; integrates with Claude Code/Codex/Gemini/Copilot/OpenCode/Cursor harnesses and with Slack/Discord/GitHub/Shortcut; MCP referenced in-session.

claims.claim: Agor brings your team and agents together on live spatial boards where you can see the work, collaborate, and learn from each other.
claims.evidence: Live boards, agent sessions, presence ('3 people on this board') and board/zone concepts are shown and documented.

claims.claim: What works for one person becomes something the whole team can build on.
claims.evidence: Shared-ownership, memory and teach-by-talking are described (teammate lives on a shared branch); aspirational and not exercised.

summary: A 'multiplayer AI' workspace that puts team and agents on one shared board — strong operate/governance thinking and a real agent surface, with the usual unknowns of an unexercised product.
